title: In our image (Genesis 1:26–31)
hookLine: male and female, made in God's image and blessed

lines: A KING'S STATUE IN THE SQUARE.
cards: In the ancient Near East, a king could set up a statue of himself in a city he ruled: carved stone, his face, in the square. It said: this place belongs to me, and I rule here, even when I'm far away.
A king's image had a job. Hold that picture, and read the end of the sixth day. God has made the sky, the sea, the land, every bird and fish and beast.
And then, instead of setting up a statue, God makes a person. These lines are where the Bible says what a human being is.

teach.b: Until now, God's commands have run let there be, let the waters, let the earth. Now: "Let us make man to our image and likeness."
Jewish readers have explained the plural in several ways, a royal we, or God speaking with the heavenly court. Some Church Fathers heard in it a hint of the Trinity.
Either way, the story slows down, as if this one matters differently.

teach.h: MALE AND FEMALE, BOTH IN THE IMAGE.
teach.b: Then the line itself, in the Douay-Rheims: "to the image of God he created him. Male and female he created them." Both. Not the man in the image and the woman a step behind.
The Catechism says man and woman are created with equal dignity, each in their own way an image of God. And what does an image do?

teach.h: AN IMAGE STANDS IN FOR SOMEONE.
teach.b: Like the king's statue, it stands in for someone. Humans are given the care of the earth, to rule it the way God would, which the Church reads as stewardship, not plunder.
The Catechism says this is why every person has the dignity of a person: not something, but someone, capable of knowing and loving God. Last, the blessing.
God blesses them, gives them every seed-bearing plant for food, looks at all of it and calls it very good.

The Catechism builds on this line; it's at the root of the Church's teaching on the dignity of every human life, from the very small to the very old, the stranger, the prisoner, the person nobody looks at twice.

teach.h: TO THE IMAGE OF GOD HE CREATED HIM.
teach.b: Each one, an image of God set down in the world.

how: Catholic teaching on human dignity, from the Catechism to the Church's social teaching, starts from Genesis 1:27, and the passage is among the readings couples can choose for a Catholic wedding.

games.why: "Let us make man to our image and likeness." the story pauses, and makes humans as God's image, male and female.

practice: Pick one face: a photo on your phone, a person across the room, or your own in a mirror or a dark screen.
Look slowly, the eyes, the lines, the tiredness or the brightness, without judging, and let the old line sit over it: made in the image of God.
If it's a face you find hard to love, stay a little longer; if you pray, ask to see that person the way God does.

wordCard.voice: Imago Dei, the image of God: Genesis says every human being, male and female, is made in it, and blessed. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: image, the word used for a carved figure or statue. Latin imago.

carryVoice: Your line: made like him. Every face you meet is someone, not something. Until tomorrow.
